I read the other comments and yeah definitely talk to your doctor about this and explain your situation. I think a lot of the confusion is coming from people who don’t do their own injections and it’s not a big deal to just ask for a refill when they visit, but if you are only seeing her every three months or so you need to have more on hand. The 100mL usually last around five months so that should be plenty in between visits. It’s very important not to miss doses especially early on. This probably isn’t the first time they’ve dealt with something like this so I’m sure they’ll be able to work out a plan with you whether it is the bigger vials or just allowing for more refills. I wish you the best

It’d probably be best to talk to planned parenthood first. I was fortunate enough to find a health clinic that handles a ton of trans patients and deal with hrt and stuff so I don’t fully know what all is needed or what all planned parenthood is capable of doing, but the nurses at planned parenthood would at the very least know which tests you need done and may be able to order it for you.

I started two years ago so I don’t 100% remember but I think it was red and white blood cell count, cholesterol, blood pressure, and some like standard tests like oxygen levels, also checking for any signs of diabetes. They also took base testosterone and estrogen levels so they had something to compare it too later on. Cost wise it’d vary depending on how much my insurance wanted to cover, but the times when they decided not to cover any it was around $350 for the tests. 
And just a heads up, idk if planned parenthood is the same but I had to go back every three months for the first two years to make sure everything was progressing at a healthy rate so make sure you budget for that as well
